transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2029-03-20
Start: 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~47 minutes
Attendees: Markus Chen (Redwood AE), Priya Nair (Redwood SE), Dana Li (Redwood CSM), Dr. Lena Ortiz (Aquifer), Samir Patel (Aquifer), Jorge Ramirez (Aquifer), Clara Wu (Aquifer CTO)

Auto-summary (auto): quick run of console, focus on per-route economics and pilot options.

Transcript:
[00:00] Markus (Redwood): Hey everyone, thanks for joining — I'm Markus, AE on this account, gonna run through the console view, Priya will jump into the technicals and Dana will cover onboarding and next steps. Um, quick check: does anyone need anything special in the agenda?
[00:18] Clara (Aquifer): No, this looks good. We're mainly focused on cost mapping to our product routes and the Dedicated pilot timing.
[00:28] Markus: Great. High level we want to show route-level telemetry, per-model cost, and the optimize suggestions — batching and quant profiles — and then talk pilot.
[00:45] Priya (Redwood SE): I'll share my screen in a sec, but quick note: the route tagging we show maps to your API route names or any custom tags you push. So you can break out by product, customer tier, or endpoint.
[01:05] Jorge (Aquifer): When you say "map" — is that in the billing export CSV? We need it for internal chargeback to product teams.
[01:12] Priya: Yes, the billing CSV includes route_id, route_name, model_variant, token counts and cost per token line. We also include a breakdown of quantization savings and batching impact per route in the export.
[01:26] Samir: Quick question: our traffic has a heavy skew — 70% of requests are short-chat completions but 30% are long-form clinical notes. How does the console separate costs for those?
[01:36] Markus: We slice by typical seq length buckets. The UI shows distribution histograms and you can pivot to avg tokens per request per route. So long-form routes surface as long tail in cost.
[01:49] Dr. Lena: Is there any automated recommendation to move certain routes to cheaper model quantizations? We care about fidelity for notes but maybe summaries can use quantized models.
[01:58] Priya: Yes — under "Optimize" we have model recommendations per route: suggested quant level (e.g., 8-bit or 4-bit), batching thresholds, and expected cost delta and quality risk. It's heuristic plus you can run shadow tests.
[02:15] Markus: We just deployed a customer who saved ~37% on their per-token spend by moving 2 high-volume routes to 8-bit quant and batching small requests.
[02:26] Jorge: Nice — what's the latency delta on p95? Our SLO is 200ms for interactive flows.
[02:32] Priya: For short requests, batching can add ~15–40ms at the 95th when batch window is 10–20ms. For many interactive routes you can set route policies to keep latency priority and still get caching benefits.
[02:47] Clara: Can we force particular routes to never batch? We have some external regulatory flows.
[02:52] Priya: Yes, route-level policy allows latency SLO and batching disabled flags.
[03:02] Markus: I'll flip to the console now. (screen share noise) Sorry if the resolution is low. Okay first panel — org overview — you can see spend trend, tokens per minute and average cost per 1k tokens.
[03:28] Markus: Jumping into routes view — here are your top 12 routes by spend. Notice the sparkline, avg tokens, and the cost breakdown column which shows model cost, quant delta, and infra amortization.
[03:43] Samir: That infra amortization — is that an RPU we calculate or something we provide?
[03:48] Priya: We give a default infra amortization estimate based on model type and instance usage but you can override with your internal cost per GPU hour so the console recalculates your cost per token with your numbers.
[04:03] Jorge: So we can do chargeback with our own compute rates. Good.
[04:08] Dr. Lena: I see a thing labeled "KV cash" in the notes — what's that?
[04:12] Priya: (laughs) Sorry that's the transcriber — meant to be "KV cache" — that's our key-value cache for mid-conversation state which reduces repeated context send.
[04:22] Markus: Also note the prefix caching section — if you have long repeated templates we surface saving opportunity.
[04:28] [05:00] (10 second silence while screen changes)
[05:10] Priya: Now clicking into one route — you get a timeline of tokens, cost per day, percentile latency, and a model variant comparison tab. In this tab we show side-by-side p50/p95 for each variant plus token cost difference.
[05:28] Samir: How are you getting model p95 numbers — is that from Redwood logs or our instrumentation?
[05:34] Priya: It's stitched from Redwood's telemetry plus the optional SDK hooks you can enable for request-level SLOs. For private deployments you can configure the collector to forward metrics to your monitoring too.
[05:46] Markus: Quick pause — any blockers on the security or data residency side?
[05:52] Clara: Yes we have PHI. We need to vet KMS/HSM flows, where audit logs live, retention periods and whether dedicated pools can be in our VPC.
[06:03] Dana (Redwood CSM): We have a Private offer that includes VPC options and HSM/KMS integrations — we can share the SOC2/ISO packet and the private deployment checklist after this call.
[06:14] Dr. Lena: Also latency for clinical note generation is more tolerant, but please show the model rollouts. We want canary to a smaller model first.
[06:23] Priya: Absolutely — rollout tab supports canary % by route, A/B test and automatic fallback if latency or error rates spike.
[06:32] Markus: Back to the cost breakdown — for this route you can toggle to "attribution" which splits cost across product tags, customers and models. If you need a CSV we export "route, customer_id, tokens, cost, quant_savings, batching_savings".
[06:50] Jorge: Can the export feed into our billing system directly? We want to automate monthly chargebacks.
[06:56] Markus: Yes, we have a webhook plus SFTP export or direct cloud storage drop (S3) and you can schedule daily or monthly.
[07:06] Clara: About the Dedicated pilot — how long does spin up take and what's the minimum commit?
[07:12] Dana: Typical spin up is 48–72 hours for reserved pool in hosted — for Private it's longer because of network setup. Minimum commit depends on region and hardware but we have smaller starter pools for pilots; we'll include specific options in the pricing email.
[07:28] Dr. Lena: For the pilot we'd like to run small traffic on Dedicated for two weeks and validate cost and quality. What metrics should we capture?
[07:36] Priya: We'll provide a benchmark plan — capture p50/p95 latency, cost per 1k tokens, request success rate, and quality comparison (BLEU-like or human evals for sensitive routes).
[07:48] Samir: On the batching side, what tuning knobs do we expose? Queue time, max batch size, deadline?
[07:55] Priya: Yes: batch window (ms), max batch size, and priority classes. You can also set route first-class for low latency where batch window is effectively disabled.
[08:06] Jorge: Any guidance for memory/kv cache sizing? We saw some evictions on our current infra.
[08:12] Priya: We show kv cache hit rate per route plus recommendations for cache shard sizes based on median sequence length. Also a table that suggests shard counts for different GPU types.
[08:26] Markus: Okay let's demo the Optimize tab — this is where we show suggestions across the org ranked by ROI.
[08:33] (screen change)
[08:47] Priya: Here are suggested optimizations — rank 1 is small-chat route A: move to 8-bit + batching window 12ms = est 42% savings; rank 2 is summary route B: keep fp16 but enable prefix caching = 18% savings. You can apply recommendations as a policy or run them as shadow/test first.
[09:04] Jorge: How conservative are the quality risk scores? If we apply a quant suggestion, how do we get notified if there's a regression?
[09:12] Markus: We tie recommendations to a prompt set and quality monitors; if model quality drops beyond threshold the automatic rollback triggers and you get alerting in Slack or email.
[09:25] Clara: Can the quality monitor do per-product blacklists? Eg. never auto-replace model for clinical notes.
[09:31] Dana: Yes you can attach tags or exemptions to any route or product line — the optimizer respects those.
[09:38] [10:00] (short side conversation: "we need to look at billing columns" / "I'll take notes")
[10:18] Dr. Lena: About data residency — can audit logs be forwarded to our SIEM in EU only? We're split across regions.
[10:27] Dana: Yes, for Private we can configure regional log routing; for Hosted we have EU region data locality and can forward logs via secure channels to your SIEM. We'll include details in the packet.
[10:41] Samir: For pilot, we need a list of sample traffic scripts. Do you provide a load harness?
[10:47] Priya: We provide a harness and examples — we'll also share a Postman collection and k6 scripts for load.
[10:55] Markus: Quick show of the rollout UI — you can schedule canary, see historical metric anomalies, and force rollback with a single click.
[11:08] Jorge: Good. Any mention of rate limiting / quotas? We need per-customer quotas too.
[11:14] Markus: Route and token quotas available; per-customer quotas supported via customer_id tag. You can throttle or block.
[11:24] Clara: Security question — is key management integrated with our KMS? We can't have keys held by vendor for PHI.
[11:30] Dana: We support customer-managed keys in supported clouds and HSM options for Private. We'll attach the KMS flow diagram.
[11:40] [12:00] (some typing/clicks)
[12:10] Priya: Back to the route table — you can apply tags in bulk and then run the cost allocation job for past 30/90/365 days. We also provide change logs so you can audit when a tag was applied.
[12:25] Samir: That's helpful. For our finance team, can you show a sample chargeback statement?
[12:31] Markus: Yes I'll include a sample invoice and a per-route chargeback CSV.
[12:36] Jorge: Does Redwood integrate with our internal billing orchestration or do we need glue?
[12:41] Markus: We have integrations and customers often use the S3 drop + lambda to push into internal pipelines. We'll include patterns.
[12:53] Dr. Lena: One more on model variants — what's the story for rolling back if quality declines after quantization? You mentioned auto-rollback but we need reproducible test sets.
[13:03] Priya: We recommend storing canonical prompt sets per route and running automatic evals post-deploy; result diffs are surfaced in the console and feed the rollback triggers.
[13:15] Clara: Any compliance paperwork we need before pilot? DPA, BAAs?
[13:22] Dana: We'll provide DPA and, for PHI scenarios, standard BAA templates and a checklist for Private deployment.
[13:30] Markus: Alright let's capture next steps. Dana, can you own sharing the security docs?
[13:36] Dana: Yep — I'll send the SOC2/ISO packet, BAA template and private deploy checklist.
[13:40] Markus: Priya will own the pilot config and benchmark plan.
[13:44] Priya: Got it. I'll include k6 load scripts and a recommended batch/window config and expected metrics to collect.
[13:51] Samir: I'll send the traffic profiles and identify the three routes we'd like to pilot.
[13:56] Jorge: I'll coordinate finance for chargeback mapping.
[14:00] Clara: We'll review and get legal in the loop.
[14:05] Markus: Thanks everyone — we'll follow up with the pricing email and schedule the security deep dive.
[14:12] (meeting wraps, some goodbyes)

Notes on transcription: occasional word swaps (KV cash -> KV cache), speaker overlaps, timestamps approximate.

End of transcript.
